Blockchain / Web3 Explainer

Polygon Surges With a New Web3 ID Service

Polygon introduced a zero-knowledge proof-based identity solution designed to enable self-sovereign, private verification without exposing unnecessary user data.

Polygon has again made the news for a very good reason. The company has just introduced a zero-knowledge proof-based identity solution: a new decentralized identification service. This well-known Ethereum layer-2 scaling solution has caught the interest of the whole blockchain world. Developers can use the service built on zero-knowledge proofs to build self-sovereign, decentralized, and private identification solutions. The Polygon ID solution uses zero-knowledge proofs to ensure that only the absolutely necessary information is communicated between participants in a transaction, while the rest is kept private. In light of multiple high-profile data breaches and cases of identity theft, zero-knowledge proofs — first proposed in a 1985 study — have started gaining more relevance. In an official statement, Polygon emphasized the e-commerce sector's potential for its brand-new identification solution. Businesses in the sector are frequently obliged to manage enormous volumes of personal data as more consumers shop online. Polygon ID would enable these companies to reduce the expense of managing unneeded customer data while still ensuring the security and privacy of user information. The blockchain world has lauded Polygon's solution as a game-changer. THE IMPACT ON THE INDUSTRY Many consider it a big step toward more internet decentralization, privacy, and security. It is viewed as a crucial advancement in the overall development of the blockchain sector. Polygon ID is anticipated to have a wide range of applications. For instance, it might be used to create safe and decentralized voting systems or enhance medical records' security and privacy. The blockchain community has reacted enthusiastically. Major companies have already adopted Polygon ID. The peer-to-peer payment system DePay, the digital passport app Clique, and the token-gating platform Guild.xyz are among the initiatives already integrated. The Sandbox, a leading game platform and metaverse ecosystem, has also integrated Polygon ID.

Latest Report on LUNC Market Price as Founder Faces Legal Trouble

Analysis of Luna Classic's 1.2% tax burn proposal going live on-chain and Binance's implementation, alongside updates on Terra's legal developments.

Despite the lawsuit that led to the delisting and scrutiny of Terra Luna earlier this year, the latest update on how LUNC is faring in the market has made it to the public. The crash of the LUNC token was so devastating that it was dubbed the worst token crash in the history of the cryptocurrency industry. This incident led the company to introduce Luna 2.0 while renaming the former token to Luna Classic. The latest report now shows that the newest Luna tax proposal — the 1.2% tax burn — has now gone live on the Luna Classic network. The tax rate is set to be implemented on all Luna Classic on-chain transactions. The idea of a tax burn system was picked as a way of helping the LUNC price appreciate once again — bringing it back to its former glory. In support of the LUNA token, Binance has joined the movement. Binance is responsible for the implementation of "Luna Classic burn" during their exchange process. All USTC and LUNC Binance user deposits are directed into the Binance hot wallet and will be eligible for the 1.2% tax burn fee initiated by Terra Classic. HOW THE COMPANY PLANS TO RUN THE NEW LUNC OPERATIONS In a statement by the management of Luna, they are willing to add the 1.2% tax burn fee for USTC and LUNC. They also made it clear that this tax won't be implemented until users make withdrawals. A report from Luna Classic says that almost 6 billion units of LUNC tokens were staked on the Classic protocol following the latest V22 upgrade. In other news, it has been a difficult week for Do Kwon, Terra Luna founder. A South Korean court has directed its Foreign Ministry to cancel the Terra Luna founder's passport. They have also issued a red notice and instructed international police to arrest him.
